title: Signal Copebook — priority requests and heuristics (Mar 2026)
body:
TL;DR
This is a compact 'copebook' for Customer Success + PMs to triage incoming inference/serving requests quickly. Focus is on 1) patterns we see across customers, 2) bite-sized patches we can ship in 1–2 sprints, and 3) a lightweight prioritization heuristic to avoid over-indexing on loud accounts.

How to use this doc (notes to self):
- Read the 6 headline asks below; each maps to a recommended owner and an estimated cost bucket.
- When filing a ticket, reference the cluster id (e.g., CL-03 latency-fallback) so we can aggregate.
- Use the small patches as temporary mitigations while PMs scope larger product work.

Methodology:
- Inputs: CS support threads (Feb–Mar 2026), 1:1s with 5 mid-market customers, product usage telemetry (per-route errors), randomized sample of 80 request traces.
- Quick clustering heuristic: group by root-cause signal in traces (auth, model-fallback, rate limit, latency spikes, mismatched token billing).
- Confidence: medium — signals repeat but we still need more telemetry on private deployments.

Voice clusters (high-level):
1) Billing surprises (freq high, business impact med-high)
   - Frequent notes about token accounting when using streaming + function-calls.
   - Customers see higher-than-expected tokens for multi-tool workflows.

2) Latency tail with batched workloads (freq med, impact high for PLG experiences)
   - Small requests in rapid succession sometimes get pushed into large batches and wait for batch fill-window.

3) Model fallbacks and deterministic quality regressions (freq med, impact high)
   - Customers observed fallback to older quantized variants with visible output quality drop.

4) Private deployment onboarding friction (freq low, impact high)
   - Networking/KMS misconfig + opaque logs.

Representative quotes (verbatim snippets from threads):
- "We were billed for 3x tokens than expected when our orchestration called the streaming endpoint plus post-processing." — integration lead, edutech startup
- "Some of our short completions took 400ms but some took 2.3s for the same prompt shape — tough to trust SLAs." — infra eng, fintech
- "After the fallback, the hallucination rate jumped — we couldn't pin it to anything we changed." — data scientist, marketing SaaS

Top 6 requests + recommended playbook (owner, effort):
1) Clear streaming token accounting examples + sample code (owner: developer-ex, effort: small)
   - Deliverable: 1-page snippet showing token math for streaming + function calling (JS/Python).
   - Quick patch: add a 'estimated_tokens' field in streaming response metadata for preview (experimental flag).

2) Per-route batching knobs and a 'prefer-low-latency' toggle (owner: serving-runtime, effort: medium)
   - Idea: route-level override that reduces batch window and caps batch size for sensitive routes.
   - Quick patch: add a per-route header (x-redwood-latency-preference: low) that bypasses some batching heuristics.

3) Fallback transparency and quality tags (owner: platform-engineering, effort: medium)
   - Add metadata on responses that indicates 'fallback-source' and model-variant confidence.
   - Quick patch: emit a short event to Audit log + notify route owners when fallback occurs >5% over 30m.

4) Private deploy onboarding checklist + debug bundle (owner: private-deployments, effort: small)
   - Checklist with common firewall/KMS pitfalls, and a one-button 'collect debug bundle' script that gathers logs and env info.
   - Quick patch: surface the checklist in the Console under Private > Diagnostics.

5) Token-usage SLA and alerting for unusual per-request consumption (owner: product-hosted-api, effort: large)
   - Long-term: introduce anomaly detection on per-api-key token rate and auto-throttle with alerts.
   - Interim: add a daily digest for heavy consumers highlighting outlier requests.

6) Test harness for fallback/regression checks (owner: applied-ml, effort: large)
   - Build a small eval suite that runs the customer prompt set across candidate model variants and surfaces divergence.
   - Interim: offer customers an 'eval snapshot' export they can run locally.

Quick patches prioritized (1–2 week shipping candidates):
- Streaming token snippet + experimental estimated_tokens field (1 week).
- Console checklist and 'collect debug bundle' (1 week).
- Per-route header to bias batching heuristics (2 weeks, guarded behind a flag).

Risk notes and tradeoffs:
- Adding 'estimated_tokens' risks surface of inaccurate numbers; mark experimental and show calculation assumptions.
- Bypassing batching reduces throughput and increases cost — must be opt-in per route and visible in cost analytics.
- Emitting more fallback telemetry increases log volume; add sampling and rollup counters rather than full trace dumps.

Open questions (needs PM + Eng sync):
- What is the acceptable latency vs cost tradeoff for the 'prefer-low-latency' toggle? (Quantify with sample workloads.)
- How should we define a 'fallback' in the metric layer (binary flag vs continuous quality delta)?
- Which customers get early access to per-route batching and how do we onboard them?

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Aisha: draft streaming token snippet and open PR for small Console copy changes — target 2026-03-22.
- Marco: spike per-route header implementation and measure p99 impact — target 2026-03-29.
- Tanya: create private deploy checklist and demo 'collect debug bundle' — target 2026-03-21.
- PM sync: schedule 30m on 2026-03-18 to align product tradeoffs (invite: eng leads + customers with open tickets).

Appendix — raw fragments pulled from threads (unedited):
- "we got billed 2k extra in one day because async postprocess kept calling the streaming endpoint again"
- "fallback happened during peak, we couldn't repro locally bc we run quantized variant"
- "can you add an endpoint that returns our last 24h top-consuming requests?"

Notes to CS colleagues:
- If you see the phrase 'billing surprise' in a ticket, tag CL-01 in the subject line.
- Use existing templates but add the cluster id to ticket metadata (helps us roll-up).
- This doc is intentionally terse — for longer writeups we will link the playbook page above.

End of file.
